messages:
From: Sung Park <sung.park@finpay.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-10T08:12:00-05:00
Subject: Severe latency affecting payment processing - urgent

Rachel —

We started seeing significant increases in tail latency on the Hosted API starting ~07:45 PST this morning. Our payment batch jobs and a subset of real-time flows are experiencing timeouts and elevated p99s (~1.1s+), and error rates have crept from 0.2% to 2.8% in the last 30 minutes. Throughput is fine overall but the spike in tail is causing retries and downstream failures.

Sample request ids: req_20260210_4483, req_20260210_4492 (attached in our logs). Impact: several payment settlements are delayed and customers are seeing 504s.

Can you confirm if anything changed on your side (model rollouts, config, routing)? This is causing operational incidents for FinPay — we need a hot fix or rollback immediately.

Thanks,
Sung
Platform Reliability Lead, FinPay

Team — quick update from runtime telemetry: we started a canary rollout at 07:40 PST for model variant \"text-gen-v2.3-quant\" on the hosted path /v1/generate. Canary traffic was ~10% A/B. Shortly after, we saw tail latency regressions on that route: baseline (pre-canary) p95 ~180ms / p99 ~420ms; on canary traffic p95 jumped to ~460ms and p99 to ~1.2s. Error rate increased slightly where queueing timed out.

Key observations:
- Regression correlates with canary window (07:40 — 08:05).
- Affected requests tend to have longer prompt lengths / >1k tokens leading to less efficient quantized kernel execution in the new variant.
- KV cache behavior: cache miss amplification for batched requests increased service queue times.

Recommendation: immediate rollback of the canary to stop any further tail impact while we root-cause quantization path and batching interactions.

I can trigger rollback now if we agree. I'll also collect diagnostics (perf traces and kernel-level logs) for INF-1723.

— Jonas
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

Thanks again for flagging this. Quick summary and next steps: 

What happened:
- We ran a canary for a quantized model variant (text-gen-v2.3-quant) at ~07:40 PST. The variant introduced a regression in tail latency for longer calls which correlated with your observed p95/p99 spikes.

Immediate action taken:
- Our infra team rolled the canary back at 08:49 PST and full rollback completed by ~08:52 PST. Metrics have returned to baseline p95/p99 on the /v1/generate route (monitoring link below).

Next steps:
- INF-1723 opened for root-cause (Jonas will attach perf traces and kernel logs).
- Postmortem and remediation plan (expected next business day) — we'll cover: improved canary criteria (tail-aware metrics), conservative rollout percentages for quantized kernels, and an automatic rollback threshold for p99 regressions.
- Customer remediation: we're prepared to discuss a service credit for the incident; Marissa will coordinate commercial remedy.

Attachments: rollback-audit.csv, canary-rollback-plan.pdf
Related: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1723 | Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.com/metrics/finpay/hostedapi/p95-p99?range=1h

Apologies for the disruption — we'll follow up with a full postmortem and timeline. Please let me know if you need an immediate call; we can get Execs on a bridge if helpful.
